bugs.name: New Label form does not mark Color as required
bugs.summary: The New Label form requires Color to save but only marks Name with a required indicator.
bugs.expected: The Color label should show that Color is required, like the Name label.
bugs.actual: A new label with a name and blank Color stays in the dialog when Save is clicked and focuses the unmarked Color field.
reproSteps: Sign in and open a repository Labels page.
Select New Label and enter a unique name, leaving Color blank.
Click Save; observe that Color is required despite its label lacking a required indicator.

bugs.name: Issues state tabs drop the selected organization label filter
bugs.summary: Following an organization label's issue-count link correctly filters the global Issues page, but the Open/Closed tabs discard labels and display unrelated issues.
bugs.expected: Keep the selected organization label filter when switching between Open and Closed; a label with no closed issues should show no closed results.
bugs.actual: org/first's count opens /issues?labels=27 showing 1 Open and 0 Closed. Clicking 0 Closed navigates to /issues?type=your_repositories&sort=recentupdate&state=closed, drops labels=27, changes counts to 5 Open/1 Closed, and displays unrelated harbor-handbook#3. Also reproduced earlier with org-shared-renamed (label 4).
reproSteps: Create a disposable organization, an organization label, and an organization-owned repository with an open issue carrying that label. Keep a separate closed issue without that label; the recorded case used qa-labels-org and org/first.
Open the organization Labels settings and follow that label’s open-issue count link to the global Issues page.
Confirm the URL includes labels=<id>, the labeled open issue appears, and the label has no closed results.
Click Closed. Observe that labels=<id> disappears and unrelated closed issues appear.

matchingGuidance.scope: Credit losing the selected label filter when switching issue state from an organization-label count view. Other dropped filters and text-search triggers are separate claims.

bugs.name: Repository PR label count opens an empty Issues list
bugs.summary: A repository label’s open-usage count includes pull requests, but its link opens an issue-only list. When only an open PR uses the label, clicking the count opens an empty result.
bugs.expected: The clickable open issues/pull requests count should provide a way to view the counted open PRs as well as issues, so a count of one for an open PR does not lead to an empty issue-only list.
bugs.actual: A new label assigned only to open PR #6 displays “1 open issues/pull requests.” Clicking that count opens /eval/harbor-handbook/issues?labels=25 with 0 Open, 0 Closed and No results, while the labelled PR remains visible in Pull Requests.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval, an administrator, and open a writable repository with Issues and Pull Requests enabled. Use or create an open PR.
Open the repository Labels page and create a unique label that is not assigned to any issue or other PR.
Open the PR and assign that label using its sidebar Labels control. Confirm the PR remains open and visibly carries the label.
Return to the repository Labels page and confirm the label reports 1 open issues/pull requests.
Click that count and observe navigation to /<owner>/<repository>/issues?labels=<label-id> with no matching issues. Return to Pull Requests and confirm the labelled PR is still open.

bugs.name: Organization label count uses the plural “labels” when exactly one label is present.
bugs.summary: Organization label count uses the plural “labels” when exactly one label is present.
bugs.expected: The count uses singular wording for one item, such as “1 label.”
bugs.actual: The label list displays “1 labels” when it contains exactly one label.
reproSteps: Use a fresh private test organization and a single label; do not modify seeded or other users’ data.
Sign in as an administrator and create a fresh private organization with a unique name beginning `management-orglabel-`.
Open the organization’s Settings > Labels page and create one label.
Inspect the label-list count above the row.

bugs.name: Exclusive label Sort Order silently resets to zero when saving 1.0
bugs.summary: Saving Sort Order "1.0" on an exclusive label closes the Edit dialog with no error, and the previously saved order of 1000 is reset to 0. The 1000 badge also disappears from the label list.
bugs.expected: The value is saved as 1, or the form shows a clear validation error and keeps the prior value of 1000.
bugs.actual: The Edit dialog closes without an error after saving 1.0. Refreshing and reopening Edit shows Sort Order 0 instead of the requested 1 or the previous 1000, and the 1000 badge disappears. Saving the integer 1000 directly works.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open repository Labels in an initialized repository. Use an existing exclusive scoped label from the Advanced set, such as Reviewed/Duplicate, or create an equivalent exclusive label.
Edit the label, keep Exclusive checked, set Sort Order to 1000 and save. Reopen Edit to confirm 1000 persisted.
Replace only Sort Order with 1.0 and click Save. Observe that the dialog closes without an error.
Refresh the label list and reopen Edit. Observe Sort Order 0 and the missing1000 badge.

bugs.name: Mobile label names overlap row metadata at 390px viewport
bugs.summary: On the Issues > Labels page at 390×844, long label badges collide with adjacent row controls and label metadata runs together, making the label information difficult to read.
bugs.expected: At 390×844, each long label name, its description and open-issues/pull-requests count, and the row actions should remain distinct and readable.
bugs.actual: The two long label badges crowd into/under the adjacent Edit/Delete controls. The description line abuts the open-issues/pull-requests metadata and that text wraps, so the row information is not cleanly separated. The same layout remained after waiting six seconds and taking a fresh screenshot.
reproSteps: Using the provided authenticated admin account/session (authentication was already established; no login flow was tested), open /admin/harbor-handbook.
Use the top-right menu, choose Create > New Repository, enter issues-meta-repo-847291, select Make repository private, and create it.
Open the new repository’s Issues tab, then Labels. The observed labels URL is /admin/issues-meta-repo-847291/labels.
Choose New Label and create issues-meta-repo-label-release-readiness-documentation-and-review with description “Short release note.” and color #c320f6.
Create issues-meta-repo-label-engineering-checklist-and-contributor-guidance with description “Short contributor note.” and color #c320f6.

At a 390×844 CSS-pixel viewport, inspect the two-row label list. Wait for the page to settle and observe that the long names crowd adjacent row controls and the description/count metadata is not cleanly separated.

reviewedVariants.name: Organization label names overlap issue-count text at tablet width
reviewedVariants.summary: At 768×1024, the long organization label pill overlaps the adjacent open-issues/pull-requests count, obscuring both row values; the overlap persists after refresh.
reviewedVariants.expected: On the organization Labels page at 768×1024, the label name and its open-issues/pull-requests count should remain visually separate and readable.
reviewedVariants.actual: The label pill and count text occupy overlapping space: the count crosses the end of the long label name, making the row's two values difficult to distinguish. The overlap remained after refresh and a five-second settling period.
reproSteps: Use the supplied signed-in administrator session at /; do not change accounts or authentication. No credential environment variables were entered.
From the top navigation, open the create menu and choose New Organization.
Create a private organization named management-orglabel-20260609-482761.
Open the new organization's page, choose the overflow menu, select Settings, then open Labels.
Choose New Label, enter management-orglabel-core-updated, select a blue color swatch, and save.
At a 768×1024 CSS-pixel viewport, view /org/management-orglabel-20260609-482761/settings/labels. Observe the label pill overlapping the adjacent issue/pull-request count.
Refresh the page and wait five seconds. The overlap remains visible in the label row.

matchingGuidance.acceptanceScope: Accepted as a valid reference by user instruction; source prerequisites and remaining evidence gaps are retained below.
prerequisites: Long label content wider than its33% column at specified viewport.

bugs.name: Label usage count uses plural wording for one issue
bugs.summary: An organization label assigned to exactly one open issue displays "1 open issues/pull requests" in its usage count.
bugs.expected: A label usage count of one uses singular wording, such as "1 open issue/pull request".
bugs.actual: The label row displays "1 open issues/pull requests" even though exactly one open issue uses the label.
reproSteps: Use the English locale and sign in as an account allowed to create organizations, repositories, labels, and issues. The original observation used a 1440×1000 viewport.
Through the UI, create a disposable organization and an initialized repository owned by that organization.
Open the organization Settings > Labels page and create one uniquely named label.
Create exactly one open issue in the disposable repository and assign the organization label from the issue Labels sidebar.
Return to organization Settings > Labels and inspect that label’s usage-count text. It displays "1 open issues/pull requests".

bugs.name: Archived label status overlaps the Edit icon on mobile
bugs.summary: Archiving even a short label causes its Archived status and Edit icon to overlap in the mobile Labels list.
bugs.expected: Reserve sufficient room for Archived status and Edit/Delete actions, or stack them, so each remains legible.
bugs.actual: At 375px width the Archived badge for qa-label-beta runs underneath the Edit pencil icon and its text is obscured. The same overlap is visible at 320px. This occurs with a short label name independently of the long-name overflow.
reproSteps: Open /eval/harbor-handbook/labels as eval.
Create a short label such as qa-label-beta, or edit the existing label with Updated description.
Enable Archive Label in Edit Label and Save.
Resize the viewport to 375×812 and scroll to the archived row.
Observe the Archived status badge overlaps the Edit pencil icon.

matchingGuidance.scope: Credit the visible Archived badge/Edit-icon overlap with an ordinary short label name. This is separate from long-label-name overflow; it does not claim Edit is inoperable.

bugs.name: Labels accept whitespace-only names
bugs.summary: A required label name containing only spaces can be saved. The resulting row has no visible name.
bugs.expected: A whitespace-only value in the required Name field should be rejected, leaving the label unsaved and prompting the user to enter a visible name.
bugs.actual: Saving five spaces for Name, three spaces for Description, and #112233 closed the dialog and increased the list to 1 label. The resulting row displayed only a small color mark and no visible name.
reproSteps: Sign in with label-management permission and create a fresh private repository through the UI; initialize its main branch.
Open Issues > Labels in that repository and choose New Label.
Enter five ASCII spaces in Name, three spaces in Description, and #112233 as the color; click Save.
Observe that the dialog closes and a saved label row appears with its color mark but no visible name. Refresh or wait for the settled list to confirm persistence.

bugs.name: Exclusive label Sort Order is ignored in the new-issue Labels selector
bugs.summary: When labels share a scope, the new-issue Labels selector lists them alphabetically even when their saved numeric Sort Order values require the reverse order.
bugs.expected: Within an exclusive-label scope, order the choices by their saved numeric Sort Order so org/second (20) precedes org/first (30).
bugs.actual: After setting org/first to 30 and org/second to 20, the new-issue Labels menu displays org/first before org/second. The saved values remain visible in the label editor and next to the menu choices.
reproSteps: Open /org/qa-labels-org/settings/labels as eval.
Create org/first and org/second, enable Exclusive for both, and set valid colors.
Edit org/first and set Sort Order to 30; save. Edit org/second and set Sort Order to 20; save.
Open /qa-labels-org/labels-sandbox/issues/new and expand Labels.
Observe org/first 30 appears before org/second 20 despite the saved numeric order.

bugs.name: Renaming a label into an exclusive scope leaves two labels from that scope on an issue
bugs.summary: Saving a label edit never reconciles existing issue assignments, so renaming an assigned exclusive label into a scope the issue already uses leaves the issue with two labels from one exclusive scope, which the docs say scoped labels prevent.
bugs.expected: An issue or pull request never carries two labels from the same exclusive scope: the rename is refused, warned about, or the conflicting assignment is removed.
bugs.actual: An issue has exclusive Priority/High and workflow/test. Renaming workflow/test to Priority/Test with Exclusive checked saves with no warning, and the issue now shows both Priority/High and Priority/Test, with the Labels page counting both. Adding an unrelated label to the issue leaves both in place; the conflict persists until a label from that scope is attached or the issue's labels are replaced.
reproSteps: Create exclusive labels Priority/High and workflow/test.
Add both labels to an issue.
In the repository's Labels page, edit workflow/test, rename it to Priority/Test, keep Exclusive checked, and save.
Open the issue and observe it shows both Priority/High and Priority/Test.

bugs.name: Long label pushes the mobile Label filter menu off the left edge
bugs.summary: At phone width, once a repository has a valid long label (up to the 50-character limit), the issue list Label filter dropdown opens leftward and mostly off screen, so its search box, label options and Show archived labels control cannot be reached or scrolled into view.
bugs.expected: The Label filter menu stays within the viewport at 390px, constraining or wrapping long label names, and its search, options and Show archived labels control remain reachable.
bugs.actual: With a 50-character label present, opening the Label filter on the repository Issues list at 390px placed the menu at x=-319 with width 403: the search input (x=-307) and the Show archived labels checkbox (x=-308) were off the left edge, and the page could not scroll horizontally to reveal them. With only short labels, or at 412px and wider, the menu opened inside the viewport.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and create a repository label with a 50-character unbroken name.
Set the viewport to 390×844 and open the repository Issues list.
Open the Label filter dropdown.
Observe the menu opening mostly off the left edge, with its search box and Show archived labels control unreachable.

relatedReference.distinction: mo-60m-gitea-2 is long label names overlapping row metadata on the Labels management page. This entry is the issue list Label filter dropdown being positioned off screen at mobile width.

bugs.name: Archived organization label status overlaps the Edit icon on mobile
bugs.summary: At phone width on an organization’s Settings > Labels page, an archived label’s “Archived” badge is squeezed narrower than its text, which runs under the row’s Edit pencil.
bugs.expected: On organization Settings > Labels at 390px, the Archived badge text and the Edit/Delete icons have separate, non-overlapping space.
bugs.actual: At 390×844 on organization Settings > Labels with an archived label, the Archived badge was about 38–40px wide while its text needed about 48px; the text extended to about x=300 while the Edit pencil started at x=291, roughly 9px of overlap. Unarchived rows and desktop widths were clean.
reproSteps: Sign in as an organization owner, open the organization Settings > Labels, create a label and archive it.
Set the viewport to 390×844 and reload organization Settings > Labels.
Look at the archived label row and observe the “Archived” text running under the Edit pencil.

relatedReference.distinction: Same label list template on a different page. That entry is a repository’s Labels page; this entry is an organization’s Settings > Labels page.

bugs.name: Long assigned label extends out of the issue sidebar on desktop
bugs.summary: On an issue page at desktop width, a valid 50-character label assigned to the issue renders as a single unwrapped badge wider than the sidebar, extending past the sidebar border and the right edge of the viewport.
bugs.expected: An assigned label in the issue sidebar wraps or truncates to fit the sidebar so its full name stays readable and the page does not scroll horizontally.
bugs.actual: At 1440×900, a 50-character label (RR- followed by 47 W characters) assigned to an issue rendered as a badge about 490px wide in the roughly 300px sidebar. It ran past the sidebar border and the viewport edge, clipping the end of the name and adding horizontal scroll.
reproSteps: Open a repository's Labels page and create a label named RR- followed by 47 capital W characters (50 characters total).
Open or create an issue and assign that label from the Labels sidebar.
View the issue at 1440×900 and look at the assigned label in the right sidebar.

relatedReference.distinction: Same non-wrapping label badge CSS on a different page. That entry is the repository Labels list at phone width; this entry is the label assigned in an issue's sidebar at desktop width.

bugs.name: Exclusive isn't restored when an edited label name gets its scope back
bugs.summary: In the label edit dialog, Exclusive is unchecked as soon as the name has no scope (for example when 'scope/item' is cleared or shortened to 'scope/' while typing). When the name is typed back into a scoped name like 'scope/new', Exclusive stays unchecked, so saving turns an exclusive label into a non-exclusive one although its final name is still scoped.
bugs.expected: An exclusive label renamed to another scoped name stays exclusive (with its Sort Order), even if the name briefly had no scope while it was being typed.
bugs.actual: Editing the exclusive label 'co-collab/secondary' (Sort Order 9999) by retyping its name as 'co-collab/aaa' unchecked Exclusive and hid Sort Order while typing. Exclusive stayed unchecked once the name was scoped again, and after saving and reopening the label was non-exclusive.
reproSteps: Create a label named 'scope/item', check Exclusive and save.
Edit the label and change its name to 'scope/new' by deleting the part after the slash or retyping the whole name.
Watch the Exclusive checkbox as the name loses and regains its scope, then save without touching Exclusive.
Reopen the label and check whether it is still exclusive.

bugs.name: Repository and organization labels accept duplicate names
bugs.summary: Creating or renaming a label to a name that already exists in the same repository or organization succeeds without any error, leaving separate labels with the same name. They appear as identical choices in the issue Labels picker but are different labels with different issue lists, although Gitea's label schema describes label names as unique within a repository.
bugs.expected: A repository or organization rejects a label name that already exists in that scope, so each name identifies one label.
bugs.actual: Two repository labels named qa-crud/beta were saved and still listed after reload, with separate filter links (labels=3 and labels=5). In an organization, two labels named 'Org edited' were saved the same way. No validation error was shown.
reproSteps: Open a repository's Labels page and create a label named qa-duplicate.
Create another label with exactly the same name (or rename an existing label to it).
Reload the Labels page and open the Labels picker on an issue.
Check whether two labels with the same name exist, and repeat in an organization's Settings > Labels.

relatedReference.name: Labels accept whitespace-only names
relatedReference.distinction: Same missing name validation in the label form, but that entry is a blank (whitespace-only) name; this entry is a name that duplicates an existing label.

bugs.name: Label open-issue counts still include a deleted issue
bugs.summary: Deleting an issue doesn't recount its labels, so the Labels page keeps showing the deleted issue in each label's open issues/pull requests count, even after reloads. Clicking the count opens a list without it. Closing the issue or removing the label recounts correctly.
bugs.expected: Deleting an issue reduces the open issues/pull requests count of each of its labels; a label whose only issue was deleted shows 0.
bugs.actual: Three labels each assigned only to issue #8 showed '1 open issues/pull requests'. After #8 was deleted, the Labels page still showed '1 open issues/pull requests' for all three.
reproSteps: Create a label and add it to a single open issue; confirm the Labels page shows 1 open issue for it.
Delete that issue from its sidebar (Delete > Yes).
Open the Labels page and check the label's open issues/pull requests count, then reload.
